meta.title: Improve tray icon update frequency
meta.body_summary: Throttle tray icon updates to every 5 seconds by introducing an interval counter and a helper function updateTrayRunningTime.

perf_labels.notes: Small QML throttling change; bot inline comments flagged edge cases but no human review; author closed without explanation after iterating.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 42 changed lines in a single file, this is a very small edit by absolute volume, consistent with a tiny performance PR. Nevertheless, it was closed without merge—likely because the author deemed the improvement incomplete or lacked evidence of benefit.

review_details.concern_detail: Inline bot comment flagged that calling updateTrayRunningTime() without elapsedSecs causes trayUpdateCounter to never increment, potentially delaying updates indefinitely. Also noted duplicated logic and missing tests.
review_details.performance_claim: Refresh tray icon only every 5 seconds to reduce update frequency and improve performance.
review_details.rejection_signals: No human reviewer engaged; bot comments were low‑confidence nits. Author closed the PR after a series of commits that may not have fully resolved the flagged issues.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: A trivial UI throttling change still required multiple iterations and received only bot feedback. The maintainer‑author closed the PR without merging, indicating that the agent‑assisted change did not meet their own quality bar or lacked sufficient performance evidence.

detection_detail.code_reading: No human code reading recorded; Copilot bot provided inline reviews and flagged potential issues.
detection_detail.ci_auto: No CI performance tests or metrics were triggered.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No before/after timing data, benchmark, or profiler output; only a narrative claim of 5‑second throttle.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: PR was closed by the author without merge after bot comments and iterative commits; no external regression was observed.

core_change_summary.description: Added a throttle to tray icon updates in src/PiloramaTimer.qml using a counter (trayUpdateCounter) and a helper function updateTrayRunningTime(elapsedSecs, force) that calls tray.setDialTime() only when the counter reaches trayUpdateInterval (5 seconds) or when forced. The throttle is applied in the periodic tick handler and reset when the timer starts.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Only one file touched; no other modifications.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: introduced basic throttling logic with onDurationChanged forcing an update.
Made interval configurable via trayUpdateInterval property.
Refactored duplicate code into updateTrayRunningTime function.
Removed unused updateTrayRunningTime call in onDurationChanged, leaving the throttle entirely in the periodic tick handler.

review_signals.summary: Calling updateTrayRunningTime without elapsedSecs means trayUpdateCounter never increments, delaying updates indefinitely until forced; suggested passing 1.
review_signals.action_taken: Final commit removed the call, so this path no longer exists.

review_signals.summary: Hardcoded 5‑second interval is a magic number; should be extracted to a named constant or commented.
onDurationChanged handler resets counter and calls setDialTime() unconditionally, bypassing the throttle.
review_signals.action_taken: The unconditional call was eventually removed.

review_signals.summary: Running‑time and setDialTime logic duplicated; should be extracted into a helper.
review_signals.action_taken: Subsequent commits introduced the updateTrayRunningTime helper to deduplicate.

review_signals.summary: Two automated overviews pointed out missing tests and naming concerns, but no blocking request.

collaboration_trajectory: Author opened PR with initial throttling commit.
Author revised the change through four additional commits, responding to inline bot comments (converting to helper, fixing logic, removing unused call).
Two Copilot bot formal reviews appeared, flagging low‑confidence issues such as missing tests and magic numbers.
No human review or external discussion occurred.
Author closed the PR without merging approximately five days after creation.
